objective: Find the original first divisible integer and stop a while loop immediately with break.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Remainder tests and early-exit loops remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Stopping at a first match avoids unnecessary work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Bounds, sentinel choice and original-value preservation transfer to other searches.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation task explicitly teaches while with break.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Nonzero divisor and signed cases avoid misleading divisibility claims.

defects: The prompt/label claimed zero was divisible by everything without excluding zero divisors.
Junior used a flag instead of the requested break; senior used find instead of while.
Input bounds, preserved sign and early tail-read behavior were unspecified.
rationale: Define bounded safe integer inputs and nonzero signed integer divisors. Scope the zero-divisibility statement correctly, retain original matching values and preserve frozen inputs. Align junior/senior with while and break. Add negative divisor/results, signed zero, a10000-position late match and a captured Proxy that rejects reading after an early match. Existing probes already reject the absolute-value candidate; the baseline count records that rather than claiming every selected wrong was newly caught. The linear bound is worst-case, not measured from finite cases.

objective: Join exact string contents with separators through for-of concatenation.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: for-of and string concatenation remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Separator placement is a useful loop-state exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Empty strings, exact text and copying cost are transferable.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation lesson deliberately avoids join.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Whitespace/Unicode and larger separators catch hidden normalization/truncation.

defects: String domains, ownership and text preservation were implicit.
A universal linear-time claim would ignore repeated growing-prefix copies.
Trimming words and truncating separators passed old probes.
rationale: Retain all correct revealed loops and specify bounded read-only strings/separator, exact UTF-16 contents and no trim/normalization. Define a conservative quadratic upper bound in output size plus word count for repeated immutable concatenation, while allowing engine optimizations rather than claiming universal linear copying. Add whitespace/newline/emoji, empty words,100-character separators,1000-character words and1000-word lists. The existing disabled-join fixture remains; source reading confirms every supplied form uses for-of.

objective: Reverse original opaque values with two inwards indexes and constant auxiliary storage.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Two-pointer swaps remain a current basic algorithm.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: In-place list changes require clear ownership.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Invariant preservation and linear scans transfer to many algorithms.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation task states its two-index method and no full copy.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Opaque identities and unusual values prevent deep-equality-only false passes.

defects: Dense-array domain, bounds and exact opaque identity were unspecified.
Cloned swapped objects or replaced NaN values passed prior primitive cases.
rationale: Retain all three correct two-pointer implementations; the prompt permits either loop form and only forbids reverse/full copies. Specify bounded mutable dense arrays, exact original references/values, same returned list and constant auxiliary storage. Add frozen element objects/arrays, NaN/undefined/signed zero,10000items and exact empty/singleton array identity. Existing disabled-reverse checks stay. Constant auxiliary storage for supplied forms comes from direct reading, not a fabricated universal memory proof.

objective: Use do-while for bounded Boolean attempts, preserving exact callback calls and thrown values.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: do-while and synchronous callback control remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Bounded retry logic is useful when its effects are explicit.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Call counts, stopping behavior and error identity are transferable.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The foundation task restricts the callback and positive integer budget.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Arguments and exceptions must not be silently changed by a wrapper.

defects: Zero/noninteger budget behavior and callback result/error domain were implicit.
Unexpected callback arguments and swallowed exceptions passed old checks.
rationale: Specify limit1..1000, synchronous Boolean results, plain zero-argument calls and propagation of any original thrown value without further attempts. This resolves the at-least-once/budget ambiguity by defining a positive domain. Retain all already-correct supplied do-while boards. Add exact argument counts, a second-call thrown object,1000th-call success and existing failure/early-stop cases. Bound loop overhead separately from callback work; unknown analyzer estimates retain25XP.
